The signed first-moment identity follows from Σg_i=d+1. Dilation about a cut-boundary point with ratio s/H_i puts volume (s/H_i)^d U_i in the captured portion up to height s. Integration of the complementary upper-tail estimate gives dH_iU_i/(d+1); multiplying the aggregate by b gives the exact stronger bound with bΣR_i.

The cone from the cut section to its highest point gives U≥ρ(0)H/d. The factor converting Euclidean section volume into coordinate density is 1/||v_i||. Concavity of the section root between −s and levels tending to H gives the backward density upper bound, with null endpoints immaterial.

Integrating the envelope to L=H(t^(−1/d)−1) gives a−U exactly. Multiplying the equal-mass difference by s−L proves first-moment minimization. Direct integration and rearrangement give the stated residual bound and the coefficient (d−1)/(d+1) in the last inequality.
